Hi, Magics! For those seeking clarification about “official” status, here’s a breakdown pls bear with me.

“Official” status isn’t just about being active on social media, sending gifts, or showing consistent support—it’s about being recognized by the people who actually run things. In the GL/BL community, official fanbases are often acknowledged not just by the general fandom, but more importantly by authorized representatives or accredited event organizers involved in artist-related activities. This typically means direct communication and coordination with the team or organizers—for example, the organizers of Mable and Pangjie’s recent fan meetings in Macau and Manila.

Being official comes with responsibilities such as coordinating approved fan projects, handling event logistics, supporting promotional campaigns, and contributing to organized initiatives. Official fanbases often act as the liaison between the fandom and management, and may also host sanctioned events, run structured fan projects, and generally handle much of the work supporting the artists’ promotion.

To be clear, being official doesn’t mean you “own” the fandom. Independent fanbases are still very much loved and respected—they just aren’t formally recognized or coordinated with by management.

Recognition usually happens organically. From experience, organizers and fans tend to reach out to the most structured, reliable, and professional fanbases when events or projects arise. Over time, these repeated coordination and demonstrated professionalism is what establishes and strengthens official status.
